title: United States and Colombia to negotiate zero tariff after quake
seoTitle: US and Colombia to Negotiate Zero Tariff After Quake
subtitle: Measure comes after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake on August 10, 2026.
excerpt: On August 20, 2026, the United States and Colombia began talks to eliminate export taxes following a seismic tremor.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On August 20, 2026, the Solar Explosion portal is following the economic and humanitarian developments in Colombia after the earthquake. The United States government indicated its intention to negotiate a zero percent tariff for Colombian exports in light of the emergency situation.

Meeting between trade representatives of both countries

The Office of the United States Trade Representative reported that a meeting took place with Colombia's Minister of Trade. At the meeting, they discussed the situation faced by the South American country following the rise of Abelardo de la Espriella to the presidency, as well as the strengthening of bilateral ties.

Negotiation of a Reciprocal Trade Agreement

The North American entity highlighted its commitment to the swift negotiation of a Reciprocal Trade Agreement. The Colombian minister showed willingness to reach pacts that bring extraordinary solutions and generate concrete benefits for both nations during the reconstruction.

Background of the additional product tax

Previously, the Colombian president had requested the temporary suspension of an additional product tax that had gone into effect in July 2026. The taxation measure included exclusions for specific items such as coffee, coal, oil, gold, and cocoa.

Humanitarian assistance and international solidarity

The President of Colombia also spoke with the U.S. government to thank them for sending humanitarian assistance aimed at helping victims and families affected by the seismic tremor that occurred on August 10.

With information from El Colombiano.
